judgments.reasoning_cat1: The preamble names the parties and fixes the effective date as the date of last signature; nothing in it is vague or grammatically defective, though it defines the two individuals collectively as 'Consultants'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The collective definition 'Consultants' sits against Section 2.a's singular 'pay Consultant twenty-percent (20%)', raising a latent question whether 20% is shared or owed to each, but the preamble itself is not the source of the tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recitals contain soft, undefined commitments — 'future consulting services to enhance the value for the sale of the property' rendered 'upon the Company's request' — and a factual assumption about the Jasper Port 'scheduled for construction in 2023' whose contractual effect is unstated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This is classic 2.3 territory: the recital conditions consulting services on the Company's request and recites reliance on the port/appraisal, while operative Sections 2.a and 2.b make the 20% payments turn only on a sale or on realized tax savings, with no performance condition — the two point in different directions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Profit' is defined by subtracting 'reasonable expenses, holding costs and expenses relating to transactions regarding the property (i.e. donations, etc)' — 'reasonable', 'holding costs' and the open-ended 'etc' are undefined, and 'i.e.' is used where 'e.g.' is meant, so the illustrative list's scope is genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The parenthetical treats 'donations' as a deductible expense while Section 2.b separately rewards Consultants for the tax savings generated by the very same 100-acre donation, so the definition and 2.b pull against each other on how the donation is accounted for.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause switches to the singular 'Consultant' after the preamble defined two 'Consultants', leaving it open whether 20% is a single shared share or 20% each, and it sets no time or manner for payment on a partial sale.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its operation depends entirely on the Section 1 definition of 'Profit', whose deductions are open-ended, and it conflicts in number with the preamble and with Section 2.b's plural 'Consultants shall be entitled to twenty-percent'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is a comma splice joining a predictive statement ('may realize certain tax savings') to an obligation, and the trigger — 'once the risk of a federal or state tax audit has expired, which is expected to occur in October 2016' — leaves both the date and the measure of 'such savings' genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It obliges payment out of savings realized by 'Company or its principal', although only the Company is a party under the preamble, and the same donation is treated as a deductible expense in the Section 1 definition of 'Profit'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, conventional merger clause; the only softness is the limiting phrase 'in connection with Delta Bluffs', which confines the integration to one subject matter.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against the recitals, which describe prior due-diligence work and an appraisal, the clause could be argued to exclude that extrinsic material, but no other operative provision contradicts it.
